```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(dar)
set.seed(130)
```

This guide starts from individual method results. Agreement summaries and
consensus rules are optional: neither replaces the methods' assumptions or
establishes a calibrated false-discovery rate.

## Prepare a small multi-method workflow

The included real dataset makes this guide self-contained. Its unadjusted
`RiskGroup2` comparison illustrates associations, not causal effects or validated
biomarkers. DESeq2, LinDA and Wilcoxon can all execute this simple design;
Wilcoxon cannot adjust for additional covariates. For other designs, consult
[Statistical models and contrasts](statistical_models.html).

For illustration, fix an optional agreement rule of two supporting methods out
of three before examining discoveries. This is not an optimized or generally
recommended rule.

```{r fit}
data("metaHIV_phy", package = "dar")
agreement_cutoff <- 2

rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(
    ~ RiskGroup2,
    targets = "RiskGroup2",
    tax_level = "Species",
    reference = c(RiskGroup2 = "hts")
  ) |>
  step_subset_taxa(tax_level = "Kingdom", taxa = c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) |>
  step_filter_by_prevalence(threshold = 0.03) |>
  step_deseq(id = "deseq") |>
  step_linda(id = "linda") |>
  step_wilcox(id = "wilcox")

fit <- prep(rec, parallel = FALSE)
```

## Inspect the result table

`tidy_results()` exposes one row per returned taxon, contrast and configured
step, without replacing the native tables held in the prepared recipe.

```{r tidy-results}
results <- tidy_results(fit)
results |>
  dplyr::select(
    taxa_id, contrast_id, numerator, denominator,
    effect_size, effect_metric, adj_p_value, significant, method, step_id
  ) |>
  head()

results |>
  dplyr::group_by(step_id, contrast_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_returned = dplyr::n(),
    n_finite_effects = sum(is.finite(effect_size)),
    n_significant = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Use `effect_metric` to interpret effect sizes. A log2 fold change and a
difference in median relative abundance are not numerically interchangeable.
The numerator and denominator define the orientation of each contrast.
`significant` retains the configured method's decision, which can include
criteria beyond an adjusted p-value, such as ANCOM-BC2's sensitivity filter.
Missing statistics remain missing; a non-significant result alone does not
prove that every native estimate was available or that there is no effect.

`method` names the stable engine; `step_id` identifies its configuration. For
example, select two executed steps without rerunning them:

```{r selected-steps}
tidy_results(fit, steps = c("deseq", "linda"), significant_only = TRUE) |>
  head()
```

Custom DA step IDs must not collide with internal columns such as `effect`,
`taxa_id` or `sum`; use a distinct name such as `linda_sensitivity`.

## Select a contrast explicitly

```{r contrasts}
results |>
  dplyr::distinct(contrast_id, comparison, numerator, denominator)

comparison_id <- "RiskGroup2[msm-hts]"
selected_results <- results |>
  dplyr::filter(contrast_id == comparison_id)
```

For longitudinal designs, `contrast_id` also distinguishes comparisons within
visits and difference-in-differences. These hypotheses must not be pooled.

## Visualize discoveries and agreement

Select taxon IDs from the results you intend to plot. Here the selection is the
union of discoveries for one contrast, not a consensus. `abundance_plt()` uses
the same aggregated taxonomic analysis view as the modeled methods.

```{r abundance, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
taxa_ids <- selected_results |>
  dplyr::filter(significant) |>
  dplyr::distinct(taxa_id) |>
  dplyr::pull(taxa_id) |>
  head(6)

if (length(taxa_ids)) {
  abundance_plt(
    fit, taxa_ids = taxa_ids,
    contrast_id = comparison_id, type = "boxplot"
  )
} else {
  message("No significant taxa for this comparison.")
}
```

`intersection_plt()` displays overlaps of discoveries, respecting contrast and
effect direction. Overlap is descriptive evidence of agreement, not independent
validation of a taxon or a measure of statistical accuracy.

```{r intersections, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
intersection_plt(fit, contrast_id = comparison_id, font_size = 1)
```

Despite its name, `corr_heatmap()` does not correlate taxon abundances. With
`type = "all"`, it summarizes agreement in binary method decisions, including
shared non-detections. A high value therefore need not mean many shared
discoveries. `type = "da"` restricts the comparison to hypotheses detected by
at least one method and requires a non-empty set.

```{r agreement-heatmap, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
corr_heatmap(fit, type = "all", contrast_id = comparison_id, font_size = 9)
```

`exclusion_plt()` and `mutual_plt()` provide alternative summaries of unique
and shared detections. Automatic discovery plots report when no significant
taxa are available. Some automatic selections fall back to the largest observed
overlap when no taxon reaches the requested support. To plot exactly a specified
selection, provide explicit `taxa_ids` as above rather than relying on that
fallback.

## Optional consensus rules

For confirmatory work, specify the panel, cutoff and any weights before
inspecting discoveries. More agreement does not guarantee greater accuracy or
false-discovery-rate control. Strict rules can discard true signals when
components have low sensitivity or make correlated errors.

`bake()` records a rule; `cool()` applies it without fitting the methods again.
Votes are counted separately for each contrast and effect direction.

```{r consensus}
with_agreement <- bake(
  fit, count_cutoff = agreement_cutoff, id = "two_of_three"
)
agreement <- cool(with_agreement, bake = "two_of_three")
head(agreement)
```

With unit weights, the cutoff is the number of supporting steps. A taxon that
is selected with conflicting directions does not combine those votes. The
result retains the contrast, direction, support and contributing step IDs.

To plot only this rule's selected taxa for the chosen contrast:

```{r consensus-abundance, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
agreement_ids <- agreement |>
  dplyr::filter(contrast_id == comparison_id) |>
  dplyr::distinct(taxa_id) |>
  dplyr::pull(taxa_id) |>
  head(6)

if (length(agreement_ids)) {
  abundance_plt(
    with_agreement, taxa_ids = agreement_ids,
    contrast_id = comparison_id, type = "boxplot"
  )
} else {
  message("No taxa satisfy the specified agreement rule for this comparison.")
}
```

An empty consensus is valid and is not a reason to change the rule
retrospectively. Per-method results remain available in `fit`.

### Exclusions and weights

These are configuration examples, not alternative rules selected for their
discoveries. `exclude` uses executed step IDs. Named weights must exactly match
the non-excluded steps; when using weights, set the cutoff explicitly because
the default is the number of retained steps, not the sum of weights.

```{r other-rules, eval=FALSE}
bake(fit, exclude = "wilcox", count_cutoff = 2, id = "two_retained_steps")
bake(
  fit,
  weights = c(deseq = 1, linda = 2, wilcox = 1),
  count_cutoff = 3,
  id = "weighted_support"
)
```

Weights express a chosen rule, not estimated probabilities that the methods are
correct. Repeated configurations of one engine are not independent sources of
evidence.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
